findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.comment: The sanitizer bucket on the preparation line was observed to have a concentration of 0ppm of Chlorine. CORRECTED- The PIC remade the sanitizer bucket using Quaternary ammonium sanitizer tablets and it tested to be at 400ppm of Quaternary ammonium. Discussed making sure to routinely test the concentration and change the bucket if it is not at the label-recommended concentration. This should typically be done every two to four hours.
findings.citation_text: 4-501.114(A) Manual and Mechanical Warewashing Equipment, Chemical Sanitization - Temperature, pH, Concentration, and Hardness. A chemical SANITIZER used in a SANITIZING solution for a manual or mechanical operation at contact times specified under 4-703.11(C) shall meet the criteria specified under §7-204.11 Sanitizers, Criteria, shall be used in accordance with the EPA-registered label use instructions, and shall be used as follows: (A) A chlorine solution shall have a minimum temperature based on the concentration and PH of the solution as listed in the chart in 4-501.114 (A).

findings.title: Proper date marking and disposition.
findings.comment: There were containers of blue sea cream dated 5/2, which is past the 7-day allotted date-marking, that the PIC stated is made in-house. CORRECTED- The blue sea cream was discarded and proper date-marking was discussed with the operator. Ensure that any Time/Temperature Control for Safety (TCS) food items made in-house are date-marked with day 1 being the date of opening or preparation, with the item being discarded by the end of the 7th day.
findings.citation_text: 3-501.18(A) Ready-to-Eat, Time/Temperature Control for Safety Food, Disposition. (A) A FOOD specified in 3-501.17(A) or (B) shall be discarded if it: (1) Exceeds the temperature and time combination specified in 3-501.17(A), except time that the product is frozen; (2) Is in a container or PACKAGE that does not bear a date or day; or (3) Is inappropriately marked with a date or day that exceeds a temperature and time combination as specified in 3-501.17(A).

findings.title: Warewashing facilities: installed, maintained, and used; test strips.
findings.comment: The facility had a Chlorine sanitizer bucket in use, but did not have any Chlorine test strips. The facility has Quaternary ammonium sanitizer tablets and test strips. CORRECTED- The PIC stated that they will cease use of Chlorine as a sanitizer and use the Quaternary ammonium sanitizer that they have. Discussed making sure that if Chlorine is used again in the future that Chlorine test strips will be obtained.
findings.citation_text: 4-302.14 Sanitizing Solutions, Testing Devices. A test kit or other device that accurately measures the concentration in MG/L of SANITIZING solutions shall be provided.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and cleaned.
findings.comment:
The following physical facilities are observed to be in need of repair: 

1. The counter holding the tea containers is observed to be in disrepair and needs replaced or the bare wood needs to be sealed. 
2. The triple sink and the bathroom sinks are observed to be in need of being re-sealed. 

These repairs were discussed with the operator. Ensure that physical facilities are maintained in good repair. Ensure that all repairs are made to be smooth and easily cleanable.
findings.citation_text: 6-501.11 Repairing. PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be maintained in good repair.

findings.title: Food-contact surfaces; cleaned and sanitized.
findings.citation_text:
4-601.11(A) Equipment, Food-Contact Surfaces, Nonfood-Contact Surfaces, and Utensils. The ice baffle was observed to have an accumulation of pink residue on the left side of it. CORRECTED- The operator cleaned it during the inspection and was recommended to use a flashlight when cleaning it to ensure it is fully cleaned. Ensure that food contact surfaces are clean to sight and touch. 

(A) EQUIPMENT FOOD-CONTACT SURFACES and UTENSILS shall be clean to sight and touch.

findings.title: Single use/single service articles are properly stored and used.
findings.citation_text:
4-904.11(A) Kitchenware and Tableware. There were to-go containers, paper plates, and small bowls that were stored on the front counter with their food contact surface exposed to contamination. Ensure that all single service articles and utensils are stored inverted or all facing the same way to avoid contamination to the food contact surface. 

(A) SINGLE-SERVICE and SINGLE-USE ARTICLES and cleaned and SANITIZED UTENSILS shall be handled, displayed, and dispensed so that contamination of FOOD- and lip-contact surfaces is prevented.

findings.title: Single-use/single-service articles: properly stored and used
findings.comment:
4-903.11: It was observed during the inspection that there was a box of boba stored on the floor in the dry storage area. Ensure that all boxes of food and food articles are stored six inches off of the ground to prevent contamination.

 (A) clean EQUIPMENT and clean ARTICLES shall be stored in clean, dry location where they are not exposed to contamination and at least 6 inches above the floor. (C) SINGLE-USE ARTICLES shall be kept in original PACKAGE or stored in manner to protect it against contamination.

findings.title: Physical facilities installed, maintained, and clean
findings.comment:
6-501.12: During the inspection, it was noticed that the facility was in need of a cleaning in a few areas. Behind the batter station, around and on the fryer, and the floors under and around equipment throughout the facility could use a general cleaning. 

(A) PHYSICAL FACILITIES shall be cleaned as often as necessary to keep them clean. (B) Except for cleaning that is necessary due to a spill or other accident, cleaning shall be done during periods when the least amount of FOOD is exposed such as after closing.

findings.title: Wiping cloths: properly used and stored
findings.comment:
3-304.14: (A) Cloths in-use for wiping FOOD spills for TABLEWARE and carryout containers shall be dry and used for no other purpose. (B) Cloths in-use for wiping counters and EQUIPMENT surfaces shall be held between uses in chemical sanitizer at proper solution and laundered daily. (C) Cloths in-use for wiping raw animal FOOD surfaces shall be separate from other cloths. (D) Dry wiping cloths and sanitizing solution shall be free of FOOD debris and other soil. (E) Containers of sanitizing solution shall be stored off floor and used in manner to prevent contamination. (F) SINGLE-USE disposable sanitizer wipes shall be used in accordance with EPA labels. 

Ensure that cloths used for wiping cary out containers are dry. Facility has switched to disposable towels for this process.

findings.title: In-use utensils: properly stored
findings.comment:
3-304.12: FOOD preparation and dispensing UTENSILS shall be stored: (A) in FOOD with their handles above top of FOOD and container (B) In non-TCS FOOD (C) On clean portion of FOOD preparation table or cooking EQUIPMENT as long as UTENSIL cleaned with proper frequency (Time/Temp Control Form). (D) In running water with sufficient velocity (E) In clean, protected location if UTENSILS are used only for FOOD not TCS (F) In container of water at least 135F and container is properly cleaned. 

Inspector observed the facility using ice to store in use utensils. Store in use utensils according to one of the methods outlined above.
